earlier.how: each structure was rebuilt from the raw bar and dividend files by a separate checker who wrote its own version before opening the builder's script, then compared figure by figure and looked for hindsight. This was done before the data repairs listed below; it is how three of them were found.

structures.name: 1 · Core + satellite
structures.verdict: 42 figures compared, every headline inside tolerance, no hindsight. One statistic was wrong and is fixed: the share of positions that beat SPY had been counted on rounded returns (37%, now 38%).

structures.name: 2 · Trend-filtered core
structures.verdict: 39 figures compared, all agree; every spell out of the market matches date for date across all five versions. No hindsight.

structures.name: 3 · Dual momentum
structures.verdict: 35 figures compared, all inside tolerance. A same-close fill, a two-session lag and a 251-session look-back were each tried and each gives a different number, so the test would have caught a timing error.

structures.name: 4 · Volatility-targeted sizing
structures.verdict: 30 figures compared, none outside tolerance. Its labels promised a steady risk level the rule does not deliver; they are reworded.

structures.name: 5 · Level-based scaling in
structures.verdict: 39 figures compared, none outside tolerance, including the whole entry experiment (3 funds, 2 horizons, 5 methods).

structures.name: 6 · Getting paid to wait
structures.verdict: 68 figures compared, none outside tolerance. Prices after four chosen dates were scrambled and the earlier results did not move, so the rule reads nothing from the future. Its own model is too generous, which the page says wherever a modelled figure appears.

earlier.lib: 92 checks, 74 passed. None of the 18 that did not pass was an error in the trade simulator, the cash interest or the measures; they were faults in the stored data (now repaired) and conventions (now stated). One real flaw was fixed: results could differ in the last digit from run to run.

rerun.what: every structure was run again on the repaired data. 32 of the 39 versions did not change at all. The 7 that did moved in the last digit only, and only where the XLF and XLRE repairs or the run-to-run fix explain it (for example the sector core + satellite 10.10% to 10.11% a year, sector dual momentum 9.59% to 9.69%). The data panel rebuilt from the saved raw downloads is byte-for-byte the one on disk.
